category_title: English language learners who use hand-as-artifact gestures to solve mathematical charts when verbal explanation is challenging
scenario_title: Explaining mathematical reasoning using a data chart
minimal_context: Liliana is working at her desk on a paper and pencil activity, answering questions written on the whiteboard using a data chart titled 'Hands and Fingers'.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at the problem on the board. Can you identify the title of the problem?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Puts LH palm up, fingers extended, over the paper on the desk with the RH holding the pencil) mmmm, I don’t know.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay. Let's look at the math problem using the data chart. What is the answer?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (LH left up with five fingers extended and palm facing self) Because, I know what’s one plus // I know the answer. Number 3.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Shrugs shoulders up and down, with LH still up in the air with elbow resting on desk. Looks at hand, LH palm rotated out over desk and then opens palm towards her face) Because the number...
